summary: Minnesota is permissive for the roof rat. Its 'regulated animals' law (Minn. Stat. §346.155) targets only big cats, bears, and primates — not rodents — and DNR rule Minn. R. 6216.0270 affirmatively classifies BOTH Rattus rattus and Rattus norvegicus as 'unregulated nonnative species,' outside the invasive-species controls of ch. 84D. So keeping, breeding, and selling/giving a captive-bred roof rat needs no state permit. The one requirement is animal-health: importing a mammal needs a Certificate of Veterinary Inspection (confirm the pet-rodent application with the Board of Animal Health). Never release one; check local ordinances.

keep.why: Minn. Stat. §346.155 ('regulated animals') covers only Felidae (non-domestic cats), bears, and nonhuman primates — no rodents — and Minn. R. 6216.0270 explicitly lists R. rattus and R. norvegicus as 'unregulated nonnative species' not subject to ch. 84D. No DNR permit is required to keep one.
keep.governing_law: Minn. Stat. §346.155; Minn. R. 6216.0270; Minn. Stat. ch. 84D.

breed.why: Minnesota's commercial-breeder licensing (Minn. Stat. §§347.58–347.60) covers dogs and cats only; no state license reaches rodent breeders. R. rattus is 'unregulated nonnative,' so ch. 84D propagation bans don't apply.

sell_give.why: Pet-dealer protections (Minn. Stat. §325F.791) apply to dogs/cats; no state dealer license is required for rodents. The pet-rodent care standards (Minn. Stat. §346.41) bind commercial facilities, not private breeders rehoming animals.

transport.why: Intrastate transport is unregulated for an unregulated-nonnative species. For IMPORT, Minn. R. 1721.0040 requires a Certificate of Veterinary Inspection for all imported mammals unless exempted; no rodent-specific exemption was confirmed, so carry a CVI — confirm the pet-rodent application with the Board of Animal Health. Releasing any nonnative animal is unlawful (Minn. Stat. ch. 84D).
transport.governing_law: Minn. R. 1721.0040 (import CVI); Minn. R. 6216.0270; ch. 84D (no-release).

restrictions.summary: Importing a pet rat into Minnesota requires a Certificate of Veterinary Inspection (Minn. R. 1721.0040, all mammals); confirm the pet-rodent application with the Board of Animal Health. No CVI for in-state movement.
Never release a roof rat (Minn. Stat. ch. 84D). Local city/county ordinances may add limits — check yours.
